definitions.explanation: The deepest, purest black imaginable, evoking the color of Japanese lacquer. A literary term used to describe hair, darkness, or the night sky.

examples.japanese: {漆黒|しっこく}の{髪|かみ}が{印象的|いんしょうてき}だった。
{漆黒|しっこく}の{闇|やみ}の{中|なか}で、{何|なに}も{見|み}えなかった。
examples.english: In the pitch-black darkness, I couldn't see anything.

examples.japanese: {漆黒|しっこく}の{夜空|よぞら}に{無数|むすう}の{星|ほし}がまたたき、{息|いき}を{飲|の}むほど{美|うつく}しかった。
examples.english: Countless stars twinkled in the jet-black night sky, so beautiful it took my breath away.

notes:
A literary word meaning the deepest, purest black — like the color of Japanese lacquer ({漆|うるし}). Combines {漆|しつ} (lacquer) and {黒|こく} (black).

USAGE:
- Used almost exclusively as a modifier before a noun: {漆黒|しっこく}の + noun
- Common with {闇|やみ} (darkness), {髪|かみ} (hair), {夜空|よぞら} (night sky), {瞳|ひとみ} (eyes)
- Has a literary, poetic feel — not typically used in everyday casual speech
- Often found in novels, poetry, and fantasy/game contexts

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {漆黒|しっこく}の{闇|やみ}: pitch-black darkness
- {漆黒|しっこく}の{髪|かみ}: jet-black hair
- {漆黒|しっこく}の{夜|よる}: pitch-dark night
- {漆黒|しっこく}の{瞳|ひとみ}: jet-black eyes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {真|ま}っ{黒|くろ}: completely black — everyday, casual equivalent
- {暗黒|あんこく}: total darkness — emphasizes the absence of light rather than the color
- {墨色|すみいろ}: ink black — another literary color term, slightly softer
